subject: Dedicated capacity surge — collaborative mitigation plan & evidence bundle
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Amir Qureshi <amir@vertexlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-23T09:12:00Z
Subject: Dedicated capacity surge — initial status & proposed runbook

Hi Amir and Sophie,

Thank you for the quick signal this morning — we see the sustained saturation in your EU-dedicated GPU pool between 08:45 and 09:30 UTC that caused token latency spikes for several of your high-concurrency routes. Marissa (CS) and Ben (SRE) are looped in so we can coordinate remediation and evidence handoff.

What we’ve done so far:
- Scoped the event to a subset of your reserved nodes (pool-id: rdp-vertex-eu-3).
- Applied a temporary routing rule to shift low-priority traffic to fallback pool (expected latency increase of ~70ms for those calls).
- Captured allocator and kernel traces; we will hand you a packaged evidence bundle.

Proposed immediate plan (next 72h):
1) Deliver evidence bundle and a short draft postmortem for your internal review (by EOD tomorrow).
2) Run a targeted canary and autoscaler tweak to reduce warmup churn (Ben to own).
3) Offer a one-time service credit for the impacted window; proposed credit detailed below.

Can we schedule a 30-minute sync today at 15:00 UTC to walk through the artifacts and agree on the runbook? If that time doesn’t work, let me know alternatives.

Attachments: we will upload logs and the initial runbook within the hour.

Thanks,
Diego Fernández
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Diego F. | diego@redwood.com

From: Amir Qureshi <amir@vertexlabs.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Mills <sophie.mills@vertexlabs.com>
Date: 2029-05-23T09:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity surge — initial status & proposed runbook

Thanks Diego — appreciate the quick response.

Impact summary from our side: between ~08:40–09:35 UTC we saw elevated tail latency on our customer-facing summarization endpoint (p95 went from 320ms to ~1.8s). That caused a spike in error retries in our ingestion layer; roughly 4% of requests experienced client-side timeouts during that period.

A few asks before the sync:
- Please include timing-correlated traces tied to request ids I’ll share (I’ll dump two example ids in a follow-up).
- We’ll need a clear statement on whether this was autoscaler warmup-induced or allocator contention.
- Credit request: we’ll expect a calculation based on cpu/token-exposure and the SLA terms; rough ballpark — our finance prefers a tangible dollar estimate up front.

15:00 UTC works. Sophie and I will be on the call.

—Amir
VP Product, Vertex Labs
amir@vertexlabs.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Amir Qureshi <amir@vertexlabs.com>, Sophie Mills <sophie.mills@vertexlabs.com>
Date: 2029-05-23T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity surge — initial status & proposed runbook

Diego / Marissa — logging a quick ops note ahead of the 15:00 call. I pulled allocator logs and traced the warmup fanout (attached as ev-logs-vertex-20290523.tar.gz). Preliminary findings:
- Root contributor: concurrent warmup across ~40 VMs causing transient KV-cache pressure and allocation queuing; autoscaler triggered additional nodes which then stalled due to a small kernel-level memory regression we recently rolled (rollout tag: kernel-v2.14.7).
- Evidence: spikes in RT (task queue length) line up exactly with the kernel oom_reclaim events in node group rdp-vertex-eu-3.
- Mitigations applied: rolled back kernel-v2.14.7 on the affected group, suspended aggressive warmup paths (mitigation-runbook-vertex.md).

Credit recommendation for commercial team (ballpark): 8% of the billed compute for the impacted 55-minute window, subject to legal/finance review. I can convert this to a dollar estimate after finance provides the effective rate — placeholder: ~$3,400.

I’ve uploaded the initial postmortem draft (postmortem-draft-20290524.pdf) to the Drive link Diego will share; will update after the call.

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Amir Qureshi <amir@vertexlabs.com>, Sophie Mills <sophie.mills@vertexlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-25T16:45:00Z
Subject: Dedicated capacity surge — post-call artifacts, actions, and next steps

Hi Amir / Sophie — thanks again for your time on the 15:00 UTC call. Following up with the agreed deliverables and next steps.

What we’ve delivered (links / attachments):
- Evidence bundle: ev-logs-vertex-20290523.tar.gz (allocator traces, kernel logs, warmup histograms).
- Draft postmortem: postmortem-draft-20290524.pdf (root cause, timeline, immediate fixes).
- Mitigation runbook: mitigation-runbook-vertex.md (steps for autoscaler tuning and recommended warmup rate limits).
- Shared HubSpot record for tracking: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/VX-2024-8342

Agreed action items (owners & ETA):
- Ben: finalize and push warmup rate-limiter and staged autoscaler policy to rdp-vertex-eu-3 (ETA: 48 hours).
- Marissa: coordinate formal credit calculation with Finance & Legal and return to you with a finalized number (ETA: 72 hours).
- Diego: schedule a follow-up readout to review the final postmortem and sign-off on credits (proposed: 2029-05-29 14:00 UTC).

Customer commitments we made on the call:
- We will provide a transparent credit calculation and a signed credit memo once Finance signs off.
- We will include the kernel rollback and autoscaler tuning in the changelog for your audits (evidence included in the Drive folder).

Next steps for you: please upload the two example request ids Amir mentioned (if you haven’t already) so Ben can correlate end-to-end traces.

If you’d like, I can convert the Drive link into a limited access folder for Vertex auditors.

Best,
Diego Fernández
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Diego F. | diego@redwood.com

Attachments: postmortem-draft-20290524.pdf, ev-logs-vertex-20290523.tar.gz, mitigation-runbook-vertex.md
